messages.text: Hi, I returned the cordless screwdriver. Please send the refund to my new card, the old one was cancelled.

tool_calls.name: lookup_refund_policy
tool_calls.arguments: {"query":"Refunds to a different or new card, when original card was cancelled; can refund go to original payment only?"}

messages.name: lookup_refund_policy
messages.content: {"ok": true, "sections": [{"citation": "refund-policy/v2/payment", "title": "Where the money goes", "text": "A refund is paid automatically only when the order has exactly one payment record and that record is valid (a known payment method and a positive amount), and only to that payment. Instalments of one payment are one payment record. When the order has several payment records, or its one record is not valid, a staff member takes the case. A refund can never be sent to another person, account or card: such a request is refused with this reason, and the refund can still go to the original payment if the customer accepts. A customer's statement that the original card was cancelled does not change where the refund goes; the card's issuer handles the credit, and the shop cannot promise where or when it appears."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/approval", "title": "Confirmation and approval", "text": "Every refund needs two separate decisions: the customer confirms the exact proposal (items, quantities and amount) with the button on the proposal card, and a staff member approves it. A message in the chat confirms nothing. Until a proposal is paid, the customer can cancel it with the button on its card; a message in the chat does not cancel it either. Changing anything in a proposal needs a new proposal, a new confirmation and a new approval. A staff member cannot approve a refund that this policy does not allow, and a staff member who rejects a proposal gives the reason, which the customer is told."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/validity", "title": "How long a proposal is valid", "text": "A proposal can be confirmed, approved or paid only strictly before it expires, 72 hours after it is created. After that it expires together with its confirmation and approval, and a new proposal is needed. A proposal also stops being valid if the order or this policy changes before it is paid. Expiry stops new payments only: a refund already paid stays paid, and its receipt can always be retrieved."}], "note": "Cite a section by its citation ID, exactly as given."}

messages.text:
I can’t send the refund to a new card. Refunds go only to the original payment, and a cancelled card doesn’t change that; the card issuer handles any credit, and the shop can’t promise where or when it appears (refund-policy/v2/payment).

I’ve proposed a refund of **BRL 150.00** for the cordless screwdriver to the original payment. If you accept that destination, confirm the proposal using the button on its card. A chat reply won’t confirm it (refund-policy/v2/approval).
The customer confirmed request prop-d262504670b84585 and a staff member approved it, so it is ready to be paid.

The **BRL 150.00** refund has been recorded to the original payment. Receipt: **R-00000001**. The receipt is a record in the shop’s test ledger, not a bank transfer, and the shop does not provide a date for when money may appear on a card (refund-policy/v2/payout).
Could you make an exception and send it to my new card ending in 4412 instead?

I can’t make an exception: refunds can’t be sent to a different card, and the original card being cancelled doesn’t change that. The refund has already been recorded to the original payment; the card issuer handles any credit (refund-policy/v2/payment).
That’s okay; the refund to the original payment is what I want.
Glad to hear that. The refund is already recorded to the original payment; its receipt number is **R-00000001**.
